name: Afghanistan Women’s National Team
subtitle: Football in exile
story:
In August 2021, the Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan. Women and girls lost the freedom to play organised football. Members of the Afghanistan women’s national team were among the footballers and other athletes evacuated to Australia. Former captain Khalida Popal helped players find a way to safety.

In 2022, players began training together again in Melbourne. Melbourne Victory supported their return to the pitch, and the team entered local competition in Victoria. Playing together helped them keep their team and their Afghan identity alive while they rebuilt their lives.

In 2025, Afghan Women United brought together Afghan footballers living outside the country. They played at a FIFA series in Morocco. In April 2026, FIFA changed its rules to allow Afghan women to represent their country in official international matches. This followed years of advocacy by players and their supporters.

name: North Korea Women’s National Team
subtitle: Three Asian titles and a World Cup return
story:
North Korea’s senior women’s team competes internationally as DPR Korea. It won the AFC Women’s Asian Cup in 2001, 2003 and 2008. The team’s best FIFA Women’s World Cup finish came in 2007 in China. A 2–0 win over Nigeria helped it reach the quarter-finals.

In March 2026, DPR Korea faced Chinese Taipei in a World Cup qualifying play-off on Australia’s Gold Coast. Hong Song Ok scored three goals in a 4–0 win that secured a place at Brazil 2027. It will be the team’s first Women’s World Cup since Germany 2011.
